name: Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas
positioning: Non-gaming, non-smoking hotel at CityCenter in the center of the Las Vegas Strip, with a 23rd-floor tea lounge and an eighth-floor pool deck
best_for: Travelers who want a Strip base without a casino or smoking
Guests who want a spa and a quiet pool deck within walking distance of Aria, Cosmopolitan and T-Mobile Arena

facts.text: The hotel sits at CityCenter in the center of the Strip and is connected by sky bridge to The Shops at Crystals.
The hotel is steps from T-Mobile Arena and The Shops at Crystals.
Aria, Cosmopolitan and T-Mobile Arena are an easy walk from the hotel.
Rooms feature a walk-in wardrobe and a private valet closet.
Rooms are done in a desert-inspired palette of soft neutrals, warm woods and jewel-tone accents.
Hard Shake's cocktails are inspired by the hard shake method.
Zen Kitchen serves seasonal American classics.
The spa spans two levels above the Strip.
The spa has a Vitality Pool with hydrotherapy jets and mineral currents.
The spa's couples experience includes a body exfoliation, an aromatherapy massage and a private hydrotherapy bath.
There is a full gym and a yoga studio, and fitness classes are complimentary.
The hotel opened in 2009 as Mandarin Oriental Las Vegas and became Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas in 2018.

highlights.text: The hotel is non-gaming and non-smoking.
Peacock Alley, on the 23rd floor, serves Afternoon Tea, custom-crafted cocktails and bites with views of the Strip.
The pool deck is on the eighth floor, with panoramic city views, cabanas and loungers and no DJ.
Every room and suite has floor-to-ceiling windows, city or Strip views and deep soaking tubs.
Service includes personal concierges and twice-daily housekeeping.

considerations.text: Room rates include a nightly resort charge and exclude taxes.
Conde Nast Traveler finds it somewhat family friendly but better for adults.
